test_title: PYST 38: SSC CGL 2023 - English (Held On: 27 Jul 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate idiom or phrase to fill in the blank in the given sentence.**

He is rich and famous and expects everyone to ______ on him.
solution: The correct answer is **"****dance attendance."** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ __ • The reason for using** "dance attendance"** in the sentence is to convey the idea that the person expects others to constantly attend to his needs, desires, or whims. • **"Dance attendance"** is an idiomatic expression that means to be attentive, submissive, or obedient to someone in a servile or obsequious manner. (किसी के प्रति चौकस, आज्ञाकारी होना) • In this context, it emphasizes the expectation of the individual to have others cater to him, given his wealth and fame. • Therefore, the​ correct answer is Option 4.** Correct sentence: *He is rich and famous and expects everyone to **dance attendance**__ on him.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ • Tap dance like mad: **to engage in energetic and frenzied behavior, often with the aim of diverting attention, persuading others, or handling a situation with great enthusiasm or effort. (अक्सर ध्यान भटकाने, दूसरों को मनाने या किसी स्थिति को बड़े उत्साह या प्रयास से संभालने के उद्देश्य से ऊर्जावान और उन्मादी व्यवहार में संलग्न होना) • **Dead duck: **to describe someone or something that is ineffective, unsuccessful, or doomed to fail. (किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति या चीज़ का वर्णन करना जो अप्रभावी, असफल या विफल होने के लिए अभिशप्त है) • **Give a song and dance: **to provide a lengthy and often elaborate explanation, excuse, or story, especially one that is intended to deceive or distract. (एक लंबी और अक्सर विस्तृत व्याख्या, बहाना या कहानी प्रदान करना, विशेष रूप से वह जिसका उद्देश्य धोखा देना या ध्यान भटकाना हो) 3a:T1656, The correct answer is "Calender."
